title: anyone here making roblox games with AI
author: cs_cast_away_boi
selftext: I’ve made a roblox game but the one i have in mind that i really want to build would requires team. i plan on sourcing the assets and making the maps myself so i want to leave scripting to the AI to go faster. What are your workflows? Mabe there’s a better way

comments.author: SuitableElephant6346
comments.body:
Yeah, I made this completely from AI (starting with gpt 3, and utilizing everything from deepseek, o1, to o3 now). It's an infinite terrain, survival rpg, with cool movement mechanics and an infinite leveling system for your items (can enhance stats on items, making them unique, etc). Here's a lil youtube video showing some of the gameplay:

[Wall Running, Dashing, Grappling, in Land of Blocks \[Beta\]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=krw2_z0J1Ts)

:D

replies.author: cs_cast_away_boi
replies.body: wait you made *everything* with AI?  Like even the map , like terrain and hills and stuff? That looks really good. my first game was a simple obby so i’m pretty new so if it’s possible to let AI make the map that’d be great 😌

replies.author: SuitableElephant6346
replies.body:
Yes, the initial spawn location is just a chunk of terrain, with some buildings and npcs i placed. But as you explore outwards, it generates random terrain, random mountains with dungeons inside of them, and it generates random 'areas' (think towns, locations, etc). It also has a global market (think runescapes Grand Exchange), which works between servers.

  
You have slide mechanics, wall running mechanics, double jump mechanics, rope mechanics.

  
It was all written by ai, BUT, I've been programming for 18+ years so I know how to prompt to get what I need, how to place the code, where to place it, what to fix etc. But 99% of it is prompt generated code :P.

replies.body:
Amazing! I just played around with the brush and other tools like that. I guess if there’s an API for that then the AI could totally do it! i will look that up right now 😱

replies.author: Alteil
replies.body: Hello, I’m trying to create a game with AI, how did you make this? Any guidance would be useful!

comments.author: IfnotFr
comments.body: AI is great for getting started or filling in boilerplate. I use it for quick scripts like GUI interactions or teleport pads. For anything more complex like saving systems or NPC behavior, I still bring in a dev friend to review. AI helps a ton, but Roblox scripting still needs testing and logic that fits your gameplay.

comments.author: dolado13
comments.body:
I’ve been messing around with some AI tools for Roblox lately, mostly to speed up the boring parts like blocking out props or getting a quick character base. One thing I tried recently was Meshy — you can throw in a text prompt or reference image and it spits out a fully textured 3D model with animations.

It’s obviously not a magic “push button, get game” thing, but it’s handy for prototyping. I’ll usually:

* Generate the base model in Meshy.
* Import to Blender or Roblox Studio to clean up, tweak textures, or re-rig.
* Drop it into the scene to see how it feels before I spend hours modeling from scratch.

Not saying it’s the way to go, but if you’re experimenting with AI pipelines, it’s worth a playaround. I’ve already saved myself a few late nights this way.
